progress_update.summary: Extended design session continuing from session 5. We refined the execution model significantly: workflow state freezes on completion (both success and failure), result is a separate return value (same as today), links provide a status window (running/success/failed + result). Developed link semantics: collections per service type, shared ownership with ref-counted GC, optional completion handlers for flow control, graph curation by workflows before returning. Separated the RFC into three documents: State Graph & Links (focused), Channels (placeholder), and Future Design Ideas (parked concepts). Session ended discussing docs directory cleanup — current structure under docs/tasks/service-macro/ is a spectre artifact, not meaningful organization.
progress_update.goal: Design the state graph and links model for Restate — making relationships between objects and workflows explicit, workflow progress observable, and computation graphs inspectable and retainable as data products.
accomplished: Refined execution model: workflow state freezes on completion (success AND failure), result is separate return value, both immutable after completion
Designed link semantics: status window (running/success/failed + result), collections by service type, shared ownership (multiple linkers, ref-counted GC), completion handlers for flow control
Established workflow graph curation: workflows clean up children before returning, retained graph is queryable via link, separate from result value
Split RFC into 3 docs: rfc_state_graph_and_links (focused), rfc_channels (placeholder), future_design_ideas (parked supervision, backpressure, reactive edges, etc.)
Produced comprehensive gap analysis between old RFC and current thinking, identified everything that was out of date

decisions: Workflow state freezes on completion (both success and failure). Result is a separate return value, same as Restate works today.
Links provide status window: running/success/failed + result. Completion handlers are optional for flow control.
Multiple objects can link to the same entity — shared ownership with ref-counted GC. Spawner is not special.
Workflow graph is separate from result. Children and state retained via links regardless of return value. Workflows curate graph before returning.
The retained graph is a first-class data product (learning, analytics, visualization, reporting), not just debugging.
Object's API surface is purely domain — no plumbing handlers needed for receiving workflow results.
Separated into 3 RFCs: State Graph (focused), Channels (placeholder), Future Ideas (parked)

continuity.arc_goal: Sessions 1-3 built SSE infrastructure. Session 4 pivoted to vision (OTP comparison, original RFC). Session 5 critiqued and refined (edges vs channels, four-node taxonomy). Session 6 deepened the execution model (workflow state lifecycle, link semantics, graph curation, shared ownership) and separated into focused RFCs. The design is now grounded in concrete semantics rather than OTP analogy.
